s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution
salient_findings: Intensely pruritic skin lesions on anterior thighs
Lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and purpuric edges
Symmetric, mirror-image distribution on anterior thighs
key_facts: 6-year-old girl with no relevant medical history
Lesions first appeared 2 weeks earlier in recurrent 3-day outbreaks
Lesions resolve spontaneously without residual injury
No systemic symptoms
No preceding infection, topical exposures, sunburn, bites, animal contacts, or recent medications
Laboratory studies within normal limits
Negative serologies for various infections
Unremarkable chest radiograph
Lesions are well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic targetoid morphology

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology of lesions

shortlist.label: Urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: Intensely pruritic skin lesions with recurrent outbreaks

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric edges and symmetric distribution of lesions

shortlist.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric edges and characteristic morphology of lesions

raw.rationale: The lesions' annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and the lack of systemic symptoms or preceding infections are consistent with Erythema annulare centrifugum, a condition characterized by recurrent, self-limiting, ring-shaped eruptions.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Typically associated with target lesions and often preceded by infections or medications, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Urticaria
rejected.why: Usually presents with wheals that are more transient and migratory, not well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: Typically involves more systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
rejected.why: Characterized by palpable purpura, abdominal pain, and arthritis, which are not mentioned in the vignette
